title: AI Funding Fears Deepen as Tech Correction Drags on Risk Assets
content:
The market's defining story stayed AI, but the fault line shifted from valuations to financing — the debt, capex and leadership underpinning the buildout. What began as a valuation wobble hardened into a broad derating as investors questioned whether the spending would ever earn its return.

The selling intensified across the window. The Nasdaq 100 fell roughly **11%** from its early-October peak into correction, and a single early-November session saw the index drop near **6.4%** as Nvidia shed about **9%**, erasing its gains for the year. A mid-November leadership shock at Nvidia then deepened the rout, while scrutiny of **circular financing** between chipmakers, neoclouds and hyperscalers sharpened funding worries.

It mattered because AI is the index: the drawdown lifted volatility, pressured credit and set the tone for all risk assets. Nvidia's earnings and sustained capex funding are the swing factors into year-end.

title: Hot CPI Reignites Fed Hikes, Driving 10-Year Yields Back Above 5%
content:
The higher-for-longer regime hardened into an outright hawkish turn. A hotter-than-expected October CPI — rising **0.4%** on the month with broad core-services strength — combined with hawkish Fed commentary to convince markets the tightening cycle has further to run.

Rates repriced sharply. The 10-year Treasury yield pushed back above **5%** towards **5.15%**, the 2-year jumped around **34bp** on the week, and USTs suffered their steepest weekly sell-off since April 2025. Futures moved to price a December rate rise as all but certain, with some houses flagging a further move in early 2027.

The theme sat at the centre of everything: elevated real yields pressured the richest equities, weighed on gold and underpinned the dollar, while keeping the long-end **term premium** alive. Incoming inflation data and the December decision remain the pivotal catalysts into year-end.

title: Surging Real Yields Lift the Dollar and Sink Gold to One-Year Lows
content:
The surge in real yields powered a decisive turn in currencies and metals, unwinding 2026's popular **debasement hedge**. As rate-hike bets built, the USD climbed to around a nineteen-month high, draining the appeal of non-yielding assets.

Precious metals bore the brunt. Gold slid for successive sessions to a one-year low near **$3,850**, leaving it down roughly **10%** year-to-date, while silver's retreat was far steeper. The move reflected higher carrying costs and a firmer dollar rather than any easing of inflation anxiety — if anything, hot prices and dearer oil deepened it.

It mattered as a regime signal: the haven bid that defined much of the year rotated towards cash and short-dated paper, pressuring emerging-market and commodity-linked currencies. With the dollar's path tied to the Fed, further hawkish surprises would extend the **strong-dollar** squeeze across global assets.

title: Gulf Risk Premium Drains as Crude Retreats From Multi-Month Highs
content:
Crude's direction flipped as the Gulf **risk premium** drained away. The supply shock that had driven Brent to multi-month highs faded as diplomatic efforts to end the regional conflict circulated and transit fears eased, turning energy from an inflation threat into a disinflationary offset — at the margin.

The price action was clear. Brent fell roughly **10%** over the month from highs near **$117** to the mid-**$90s**, touching a ten-week low before a modest bounce as peace hopes wavered. European gas also softened, broadening the relief across the energy complex.

Yet the reprieve stayed fragile and incomplete. With core-services inflation, not energy, now driving the price data, cheaper crude offered only limited cover for central banks. Any renewed flare-up around the Strait of Hormuz remains the key upside tail for both oil and the broader inflation outlook.
